Wildlife

Forty-one creatures, built from ARK skeletons

Every creature keeps its original ARK bone hierarchy and animation clips, rebuilt as Minecraft cuboids and rendered with GeckoLib. Five coloured skin variants each, herds, hunters, nests, sea creatures and cold-climate species. The pips show the first danger rank where each one appears.

World

A map with hidden danger

The Overworld repeats five equal-area danger zones in a symmetric grid. Curved borders make the pattern feel random on foot. The zone decides which species spawn and how strong they are. Players only see it through the Xaero map overlay, and that overlay can be locked until the tribe tames a creature from a rank-5 zone. This map runs the same formula as the mod. Drag to pan, scroll to zoom.

Move over the map

Habitats

Danger and wild levels come only from the zone. The biome decides which community lives there: warm species share every temperate biome, the snow, the wetlands and the sea keep their own residents, and flyers nest over any land. Spawn-list weights are split across each habitat, so wider habitats bring variety, not more animals.

Land habitats

Herds keep home ranges near water, predators patrol and hunt, and populations recover per habitat without forcing chunk loads.

Flyers and nests

Each flyer keeps one local nest on cliffs or shores. It perches, forages and returns home, and its eggs can be collected.

Sea and swamp

Sea creatures keep saved home pools. Crocodilians and Titanoboa hunt shorelines, and cold species drink from snow and ice.

Behaviour

Animals that pace themselves

Every creature runs a two-level state machine: an intent (roam, hunt, flee, sleep, drink...) and the animation-timed action that carries it out (notice, roar, chase, look around...). How much of it runs depends on the distance to the nearest player, so a valley of herds costs little until you walk into it, and herd mates react with their own delays instead of moving like one machine.

Full detail

Within 64 blocks

Full behaviour: senses, needs (hunger, thirst, fatigue), hunting, fleeing, drinking and the timed bridges between states. Decisions twice a second.

Ambient

64 to 128 blocks

Seen from afar: short walks, turns, stops, looking around, grazing, sniffing, pooping and the daily sleep schedule. One cheap decision every few seconds; needs frozen.

Dormant

128 to 256 blocks

Culled: no routine. Within this radius the pose still follows the schedule (asleep or standing) on a slow timer; beyond it nothing runs.

Each tier border has a margin of 8 blocks, so a creature on the line does not flicker between tiers. A hit, an alarm, a target, a rider, a tame or torpor always runs full detail, and hunger and thirst only change there.

The day of a land animal

Each animal shifts its own clock by up to half a minute, so a herd dozes off and wakes one by one.

Carnivores
SleepRoamHuntHunt
Night: hunt. Morning: sleep. Afternoon: roam and drink.
Herbivores
RoamSleepSleep
Night: sleep. Day: graze, drink and roam.

State machines by model

Rows are the current state and columns the next one. A filled cell is a transition the real decision code produced in seeded encounters; hover or tap it for the rules behind it. The diagram beside it shows the same edges.

Land herbivore

landamphibious

Grazes, drinks and roams by day, sleeps at night. Startles before it bolts; defensive herds stand together at night. Alarms ripple through the herd instead of moving it in lockstep.

Land carnivore

landamphibiouspredator

Hunts at night, sleeps through the morning and roams in the afternoon. Warns before it charges: big carnivores notice, face and roar; stalkers creep in low. Pack mates react with their own delay.

Flyer

air

No day schedule, hunger or thirst. Each bird flies smooth laps around its nest (wide loops, figure eights over the nest, thermal circles that gain height), then lands, perches, looks around and takes off again. Egg thieves and, for apex flyers, intruders are circled and swooped.

Flight phases (FlyingCreatureEntity). Clips follow the motion: flap when climbing, glide when level or descending, bank left or right in turns, hover on approach. 8 states, 21 transitions

Flight curves

Progression

From a loose rock to the Iron Age

The Tribe Chronicle (press P in game) holds forty-four technologies over three ages. Each age starts at one gate and splits into its paths (four in the Prehistoric, three after), and every path must be finished to open the next age. Progress is shared by your FTB team. Hover a node for its objective.

Survival systems

Built for a tribe of two or more

Taming and torpor

Each creature tames one of three ways: passive feeding, knockout with narcoberries and tranquilizer arrows, or aerial feeding by appetite. Favourite foods tame faster, and every creature has a measured rider seat.

Weight and cargo

Carried mass shows on a HUD gauge. Past capacity you slow down, and overloaded flyers refuse to take off. Harnesses unlock each creature's hold, with one-click Load and Unload to nearby chests.

Working tames

Order a Triceratops to forage plants or an Ankylosaurus to mine stone and ore. They work only while a tribe member supervises, and they never touch blocks players placed.

The downed state

A lethal hit starts a bleed-out timer instead of killing you. A tribemate can revive you with a fiber bandage before it runs out.

Keratin and melee

Keratin makes the first armour set and the Keratin Spear. Better Combat gives every Ark weapon its own swing: the spear stabs two-handed with extra reach, knives slash as daggers.

Tribes

FTB Teams parties share riding, cargo, orders and work permissions on each other's tames, plus the Chronicle and the journal.

The First Guardian

Carry an Allosaur Heart to an Ancient Remnants monolith to wake a Guardian Giganotosaurus. It resets if you retreat and can't be farmed, and it drops the Workshop Schematic that opens the workshop age.

Night and behaviour

Creatures forage, drink, rest, sleep, flee and hunt on a day-night cycle. Carnivore eyes glow in the dark, and wild creatures grow stronger with level.

Spatial audio

Built-in reverb and occlusion, footsteps that match the material underfoot, and ambient soundscapes, all in one client-only engine.

Carcasses and cooking

Dinosaurs drop seven meat families plus leather, bone and feathers; horned, plated and beaked ones also drop keratin. Cook meat on the Stone Fire, or hang it on a rack and let it cure to Dried Meat III.

Camp and blocks

Every station is a real object

Original low-poly models built from Minecraft cuboids, with no custom rendering library. Every card is rendered from the model the game ships, with the same camera and light. Stations only work in loaded chunks, so being away never produces a windfall.

Recipe Tree

What each item needs, from bare hands up

The recipe gates, separate from the Tribe Chronicle: which station or tool opens each item. Item sprites are crisp 32 px originals or re-toned vanilla sprites; dinosaur meats are drawn larger in hand and on the ground than normal Minecraft meat.

The dependency map

Every item sits in the first column where it can be made, counted in crafting steps from bare hands, grouped under the station or tool that makes it. Hover or tap one: what it needs lights up in green, back to bare hands, and what it unlocks in blue. This is the draft awaiting approval (F12), so it shows proposed changes beside what the game does today.

Notes on the rows (49)
  1. Loose rocks lie on the ground in every Overworld biome (F02). A rock is not stone: it never turns into cobblestone. Needs a dedicated sprite.
  2. In game today: Narcoberry, Tintoberry, Amarberry and Azulberry. A grass block drops a berry 35% of the time: red, yellow and blue 30% each of that, black 10%. The food values are yours; the red berry starts the medicine path.
  3. Fiber is the primitive rope and goes into every rock tool. Today it is drawn with the wheat sprite.
  4. New item. Today leaves drop a Stick 20% of the time; that drop becomes the Twig.
  5. You set Twig → Stick; the 2 → 1 ratio is a proposal. After the axe, planks give sticks cheaply, so twigs only matter before the first log.
  6. Today this is the Stone Hatchet. It has to fit the 2×2 grid: logs need an axe, and the Working Station needs logs. Uses the vanilla stone axe sprite (B04).
  7. Knapping: one rock struck on another. The sharp flake tips arrows in place of flint.
  8. The Working Station replaces the crafting table (F14): two planks over two logs, so it needs the axe. Vanilla tables that turn up in an inventory become Working Stations.

  10. Today: 4 Fiber + 1 Leather. Nine items need the 3×3 grid, so the bedroll arrives right after the axe and the Working Station, not at step 1 (Q2).
  11. The vanilla pickaxe pattern with one Fiber in any free slot (Q3). Its mining tier decides whether copper and iron can ever be reached (Q1).

Open decisions (15)
  1. Q1Blocking

    Rock tool mining tier

    The rock set uses the wooden tier today, which cannot harvest copper, iron or lapis ore. With stone tools removed nothing past the forge can be reached.

    RecommendationKeep wood stats (speed, durability, damage) but let the rock pickaxe mine at stone level. Copper then becomes the second tool tier.

  2. Q2Spec gap

    The bedroll needs the 3×3 grid

    9 Fiber does not fit the 2×2 inventory, so the bedroll comes after the axe and the table.

    RecommendationAccept it. Step 1 stays "gather", and the first night comes after the first log.

  3. Q3Answer

    Fiber in any slot

    Yes, this works: a custom shaped recipe type matches the tool pattern and accepts one Fiber in any empty slot. JEI shows it in one slot with a note.

    RecommendationUse it for the whole rock set.

  4. Q4Spec gap

    Starter kit

    New players still get a bedroll, 2 bandages, 8 fiber and a flint knife, which contradicts "starts with nothing".

    RecommendationRemove it, or reduce it to the Field Journal.

  5. Q5Naming

    Berry names

    The chart uses your names; the game has Narco-, Tinto-, Amar- and Azulberry.

    RecommendationRename them to Black-, Red-, Yellow- and Blueberry and keep the old ids so existing worlds load.

  6. Q6Content

    One rock set

    Stone Knife and Flint Knife overlap with the new set; the Keratin Spear is now the first weapon tier.

    RecommendationThe Stone Knife becomes the Rock Sword (London node moves) and the Flint Knife goes.

  7. Q7Content

    Sedative chain

    Blackberry → Sedative (2×2) → Narcotics (mortar) replaces Concentrated Sedative, which the Medicine Bench makes today from 4 Blackberries and a Fiber.

    RecommendationTranq Arrow takes a Sedative, Improved Tranq takes Narcotics, and Narcotraffic tracks Narcotics.

  8. Q8Balance

    Twig and rack ratios

    Twig → Stick and the rack's wood + sticks need numbers.

    Recommendation2 Twig → 1 Stick; Drying Rack = 2 Log + 4 Stick.

  9. Q9Blocking

    No quartz

    Without the Nether there is no nether quartz: comparator, observer and daylight detector cannot be made.

    RecommendationAdd an Overworld quartz source (a deep ore or a geode drop), or give those three Ark recipes.

  10. Q10Blocking

    Tom's Storage can't be built

    The inventory connector, interface and wireless terminals need ender pearls. The storage terminal needs a comparator and glowstone. None of these can be crafted, so no storage network works in survival.

    RecommendationOverride those recipes in Ark data, for example with diamond, redstone and copper.

  11. Q11Answer

    Gunpowder

    Creepers, ghasts and witches are gone, but the Crusher (F14) grinds flint into gunpowder, so TNT has a renewable source again.

    RecommendationKeep it.

  12. Q12Content

    Vanilla campfire

    The vanilla campfire (logs, sticks, coal) cooks like the Stone Fire and also completes the warmth node.

    RecommendationKeep it as the coal-era option.

  13. Q13Yours

    Open design

    Blueberry effect, the Redberry medicine path and creature drops (blood, heart…).

    RecommendationLeft open, as in your spec.

  14. Q14Spec gap

    Crusher ore doubling

    The Crusher turns an ore block into two raw metal, but ore blocks only drop with Silk Touch, and enchanting is removed. Only raw metal blocks can be crushed, for one extra raw per block.

    RecommendationLet the Crusher double raw metal instead (1 raw → 2, slower), so it pays off once Q1 opens the ores.

  15. Q15Content

    Medicine Bench and the Mortar

    Your spec grinds Sedative into Narcotics and starts the medicine path at a Mortar & Pestle (B02). The new Medicine Bench (F14) already makes the medicine: Herbal Bandage, Healing Mixture and Concentrated Sedative.

    RecommendationFold the mortar into the Medicine Bench: Narcotics and the Redberry medicines become bench recipes, and the mortar model sits on the bench.

Accessories

Gear worn on the body

Every Curios slot is in use: two head slots, necklace, back, body, two bracelets, hands, two rings, belt, legs, two feet, a charm and the universal curio slot. Each accessory is a small model hung on the player's own bones, so it walks, sneaks, swims and rides with the wearer, spreads over armour, and shows on the first-person arms. Renders below come from the shipped models.

What prehistoric people actually wore, made from creature parts and camp materials: slit goggles, Ötzi's pack frame, snowshoes, bone skates, a Beaker-culture wristguard, the Ishango tally bone. The stalker set (hood, ghillie wrap, moccasins) hides each sense the creatures use: scent, sight and hearing.

Interface rework

Carved stone, moss and ember

The Ark UI resource pack re-skins the whole vanilla interface to match this page, so shaders and the menus share one look. Containers become light limestone, so vanilla's dark titles stay readable. Buttons, the hotbar and tooltips become dark basalt with moss and ember accents. Every slot stays exactly where vanilla puts it, so other mods' screens still line up.

What changes

Containers
All 26 vanilla container screens, the recipe book and container sprites
Widgets
Buttons, sliders, tabs, checkboxes and scrollers
HUD
Hotbar, selection, offhand slots, experience bar background
Tooltips
Basalt panel with a moss frame
Tech tree
Rounded eight-point star nodes that fill the screen height
Menus
FancyMenu title screen with the Ark background and logo
Inventory
Ark layout: curio slots beside the armour, shield and charm under the player (Curios fork)
Mod screens
Tom's Storage terminals and Curios screens get the same re-skin
Toggle
arkUiPack in the client config (restart to apply)

Tech tree nodes: locked, ready, complete and hover.

Integrations

Every mod in the pack, and what Ark does with it

Each integration is one row in the management dashboard. Official releases are pinned by SHA-512 and rebranded "Ark - Name" with the Ark icon and a credit line; the original license and mod id stay intact. Where Ark needs code changes, the mod is built from its own source with Ark patches (Ark/pack/patches). python Ark/tools/build_pack.py assembles everything into a Modrinth pack.

I01

World map and danger telemetry

Integratedclient
  • Ark - Xaero's World MapOfficial release, Ark-branded · All Rights Reserved · closed source
  • Ark - World Map BridgeOfficial release, Ark-branded · MIT · source
Uses
Xaero's fullscreen map, drawn with Ark's colour-coded danger zones through the bridge hook. Map access can be locked until the tribe tames a creature from a rank-5 zone (progression.mapRequiresUnlock).
Changed
No code changes to Xaero (closed source). All Ark behaviour lives in Ark's own overlay (client/XaeroDangerOverlay.java). The jar is only rebranded.
Next
P10 telemetry technology: a mid-game item or block that turns on the danger overlay, and an end-game one that adds Xaero creature detection.
I02

Spatial audio

Integratedclient
  • embedded in ArkEmbedded in the Ark jar · GPL-3.0 · source
  • embedded in ArkEmbedded in the Ark jar · LGPL-3.0 · source
  • embedded in ArkEmbedded in the Ark jar · MIT at the pinned asset commit (PolyForm Shield today) · source
Uses
Reverb, occlusion and reflections from Sound Physics Remastered; material footstep recordings from Presence Footsteps; environmental recordings from AmbientSounds. All run in one client-only engine inside the Ark jar.
Changed
Physics code ported into dev.nez.arksurvivalreturns.client.audio.physics. The recordings keep their original asset namespaces (ambientsounds:, presencefootsteps:), and a resource-pack catalog (arksurvivalreturns:audio/catalog.json) replaces AmbientSounds' engine and its CreativeCore dependency. Ambient beds skip ray tracing.
Next
Keep it embedded. Presence Footsteps has no NeoForge build, and loading the standalone Sound Physics jar next to the port would double-process sounds. Dino calls still need recordings (P02).
I03

Tribe, journal and tech-tree backend

Integratedboth
  • Ark - FTB QuestsOfficial release, Ark-branded · All Rights Reserved (FTB) · source
  • Ark - FTB TeamsOfficial release, Ark-branded · All Rights Reserved (FTB) · source
  • Ark - FTB LibraryOfficial release, Ark-branded · All Rights Reserved (FTB) · source
  • Ark - FTB XMod CompatOfficial release, Ark-branded · All Rights Reserved (FTB) · source
  • Ark - JEIOfficial release, Ark-branded · MIT · source
Uses
An FTB Teams party is the tribe: it shares tame permissions, the Field Journal chapters and the Tribe Chronicle. Invisible FTB chapters mirror the 40 tech nodes, and FTB is the authority for completion. JEI is the recipe viewer.
Changed
No code changes to FTB or JEI. Ark ships the quest pack (config/ftbquests) and the bridge (feature/tech/TechFtbBridge.java). Jars are only rebranded.
Next
B05: the tech_flow test fails (an Ark grant does not reach FTB). B03: JEI categories for the Stone Fire and Primitive Forge, and hide the removed furnace recipes.
I04

Storage network

Integratedboth
  • Ark - Tom's StorageBuilt from source, Ark fork · MIT · source
Uses
Terminals, connectors and crafting terminals that link chests into one network. Tames' Load and Unload buttons reach the network through NeoForge's item capability, like any other modded storage.
Changed
Built from source (branch 26.1) and branded. Ark's cargo transfer now reads the item capability as well as vanilla containers (GameTest integration_toms_storage). The Ark UI pack re-skins its terminal screens and widgets. No gameplay code removed: every block is cheap, and its common config caps scan sizes.
Next
Replaces the removed P04 storage crate. In-client check: terminal screens under the Ark UI pack.
I05

Menus and title screen

Integratedclient
  • Ark - FancyMenuOfficial release, Ark-branded · DSMSLv3.1 · source
  • Ark - KonkreteOfficial release, Ark-branded · Apache-2.0 · source
  • Ark - MelodyOfficial release, Ark-branded · MIT · source
Uses
A title-screen layout with the Ark background (the real danger map as contours) and logo. The vanilla logo and splash text are hidden.
Changed
Ark ships the layout (config/fancymenu/customization/ark_title_screen.txt) and the art. Jars are only rebranded.
Next
In-client check of the layout. Later: pause menu and loading screen in the same style.
I06

Rendering and shaders

Pinned, tuning laterclient
  • Ark - SodiumOfficial release, Ark-branded · PolyForm Shield 1.0 · source
  • Ark - IrisOfficial release, Ark-branded · LGPL-3.0 · source
  • Bliss ShadersShader pack, unmodified · All Rights Reserved · source
  • Complementary ReimaginedShader pack, unmodified · Complementary custom license · source
Uses
Sodium renders chunks and Iris loads shader packs. Bliss is pinned as the planned default pack; Complementary stays as the tested fallback.
Changed
Nothing yet. This is the last pass: Sodium, Iris and Bliss settings, plus Distant Horizons LOD settings, tuned together.
Next
Profile GPU and CPU (P12), then ship tuned Sodium, Iris and shader configs.
I07

Accessories

Integratedboth
  • Ark - Curios APIBuilt from source, Ark fork · LGPL-3.0 · source
Uses
Accessory slots in one Ark inventory: crown and hat (head), necklace, shirt (body), belt, pants (legs, added by Ark), socks and shoes (feet), and a charm.
Changed
Built from source (branch 26.1.2) with an Ark patch (Ark/pack/patches/curios): the inventory key opens a 212 px screen with the curio slots beside the armour column, the shield and charm under the player and crafting on the right. The separate Curios button is off. Ark's data pack defines the slot set. GameTest integration_curios checks all nine slot positions.
Next
In-client check: the screen at every GUI scale, the recipe book and the JEI overlay. Ark accessories to fill the slots are still to be designed.
I08

Terrain, biomes and distance

Integratedboth
  • Ark - TectonicOfficial release, Ark-branded · MIT · source
  • Ark - LithostitchedOfficial release, Ark-branded · MIT · source
  • Ark - TerralithOfficial release, Ark-branded · Stardust Labs License · source
  • Ark - Distant HorizonsOfficial release, Ark-branded · LGPL-3.0 · source
Uses
Tectonic reshapes terrain (with built-in Terralith support), Terralith adds 95 biomes, and Lithostitched is their shared worldgen library. Distant Horizons draws far-away terrain as low-detail LODs on the client.
Changed
Ark maps every Terralith biome to its closest vanilla analog, so Terralith biomes get Ark creature spawns and a difficulty tier (optional tag entries, safe without Terralith). Danger zones are coordinate-based and work unchanged. Jars are only rebranded.
Next
Tune DH together with shaders (I06). In-client check of spawn density in Terralith biomes.
I09

Bronze and Iron Age machinery

Blockedboth
  • Ark - CreateNo 26.1 build yet · Create Mod License · source
Uses
Planned core of the Bronze and Iron ages: basic kinetics and processing only, no complex contraptions.
Changed
Nothing yet. Create has no Minecraft 26.1 release or branch (its newest is 1.21.1), and it needs Flywheel and Ponder ported too.
Next
Wait for the official 26.1 port. Meanwhile, Bronze basics (alloying, charcoal) can use the Primitive Forge.
I11

Melee combat

Integratedboth
  • Ark - Better CombatOfficial release, Ark-branded · All Rights Reserved · source
  • Ark - Player Animation LibraryOfficial release, Ark-branded · MIT · source
  • Ark - Cloth ConfigOfficial release, Ark-branded · LGPL-3.0-only · source
Uses
Directional swings, combos and two-handed poses for melee weapons. Ark supplies the movesets: the Keratin Spear stabs two-handed with a block of extra reach, the stone and flint knives slash as daggers, the stone hatchet swings as an axe; vanilla swords, mace and trident use Better Combat's own.
Changed
Official 26.1.2 releases, rebranded only. Ark ships its movesets as data (data/arksurvivalreturns/weapon_attributes), so nothing loads when the mod is absent. The keratin spear keeps its vanilla charge on use. GameTest integration_better_combat checks the three movesets.
Next
In-client check: spear stabs and reach on dinosaurs, knife combos, the two-handed pose while riding. Movesets for the Bronze and Iron weapons as they arrive (P13).
